Vestas Wind Systems A/S Announces Major Investment to Expand Danish Manufacturing Capacity

Vestas Wind Systems A/S, the world’s leading wind turbine manufacturer, has announced a significant investment aimed at expanding its manufacturing operations in Denmark. The move is set to boost production capacity to meet rising global demand for renewable energy solutions and to reinforce Denmark’s status as a hub for wind energy innovation.

The investment, valued at DKK 850 million, will be directed towards modernizing and expanding Vestas’ key production facilities in Aarhus and Ringkøbing, with the creation of around 300 new skilled jobs over the next two years. The expansion project will include the installation of advanced automation systems, upgrades to existing assembly lines, and the construction of a new blade manufacturing hall.

“Denmark has long been at the forefront of wind energy, and this expansion underlines our commitment to delivering cutting-edge technology from the heart of the industry,” said Morten Dyrholm, Senior Vice President of Group Communications at Vestas Wind Systems A/S. “Our investment not only supports our global supply chain but also drives employment and skills development in the local communities.”

The Danish Wind Energy Association welcomed the announcement, highlighting the role of Vestas in the nation’s clean energy ambitions. “Vestas’ continued investment demonstrates both confidence in Denmark’s industrial capabilities and the strength of the wind sector as a source of sustainable growth,” said Lene Jørgensen, spokesperson for the Association.

Industry analysts note that surging global demand for renewable energy, fueled by government targets and corporate sustainability commitments, is pushing manufacturers to expand capacity. “Supply bottlenecks have been a concern in the wind sector, so Vestas’ expansion is timely,” commented Søren Mathiasen, a Copenhagen-based renewable energy analyst. “It positions the company to respond rapidly to new orders, especially in emerging offshore markets.”

The Danish Ministry for Industry, Business and Financial Affairs has expressed support for the project, citing the positive economic and environmental impacts. Local officials in Aarhus and Ringkøbing anticipate that the new jobs will provide a boost to the regional economies and encourage further investment in green technologies.

Vestas expects the expanded facilities to be fully operational by late 2025, with recruitment and training initiatives already under way. The company has reaffirmed its commitment to sustainability, noting that the upgraded sites will feature energy-efficient systems and increased use of recycled materials in production.
